input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: __aexit__ delegates to __exit__ with None for the exception type, value and traceback instead of forwarding the arguments it received
- failure path: an exception raised inside `async with attempt:` reaches __aexit__, which calls __exit__ with (None, None, None); __exit__ takes its success branch, records no failed outcome and returns None, so the exception propagates out of the async with and past the retry loop: the attempt is never recorded as failed and no retry happens

Reviewer finding
- description: __aexit__ discards the real exception details and forwards None, None, None to __exit__, so an exception raised inside `async with attempt:` is recorded as a successful attempt instead of a failure.
- rationale: Trigger: an async retried coroutine raises inside `async with attempt:`. Mechanism: __aexit__ ignores exc_type, exc_value and traceback and calls self.__exit__(None, None, None), which takes the success path (set_result(None)), so the retry state never records the exception and the exception is not handled as a failed attempt. Impact: the retry loop never retries the failing attempt, and the error propagates straight out of the retry call while the statistics report success. Passing the received exception arguments through would fix this.
critique: The finding describes the same mechanism as the label. __aexit__ passes (None, None, None) to __exit__ instead of the real exception arguments, so __exit__ takes the success path and records no failure. The exception then propagates without a retry, exactly as the labeled failure path states.
